title: Pulse and rhythm
summary: Keep a steady beat, count note values, and play in 4/4 and 3/4 time.

lessons.title: Beat, tempo, and counting
lessons.summary: Feel a steady beat, read tempo in BPM, and count bars of four.

steps.title: The beat
steps.body:
The **beat** (or **pulse**) is the steady tick you tap your foot to. **Tempo** is how fast the beats go, measured in **beats per minute (BPM)**: 60 BPM is one beat per second.

Beats are grouped into **measures** (also called **bars**), separated by **bar lines**. A **time signature** such as **4/4** says how many beats are in each measure (top number: 4) and which note gets one beat (bottom number: 4 = the quarter note).

In 4/4, count out loud: **1 2 3 4, 1 2 3 4**. Beat 1 of each measure is the strongest.

diagram.rhythm: q q q q q q q q
diagram.caption: Two measures of 4/4: count 1 2 3 4 | 1 2 3 4

steps.title: Following the visual beat
steps.body:
When the app listens, its sound is muted. You will see a **visual count-in** (one measure of pulses before you start) and a beat marker that pulses on every beat. Watch it the way you would watch a conductor.

To practice with sound, use a metronome app on another device at low volume, or tap your foot. The goal is to play **with** the beat, not after it.

mistakeTips: Start on the first beat after the count-in, not during it.
Keep counting even if one note is late; do not stop to fix it.
Rushing is common. Let each beat arrive before you play.

questions.explanation: BPM = beats per minute; 60 per minute is one per second.

questions.prompt: In 4/4 time, how many beats are in each measure?
questions.explanation: The top number of the time signature gives the beats per measure.

questions.prompt: Which beat is usually strongest in 4/4?
questions.explanation: The downbeat, beat 1, starts each measure and carries the most weight.

reviewItems.answer: How many beats are in each measure.

lessons.title: Whole, half, and quarter notes
lessons.summary: Hold notes for four, two, and one beat.

steps.title: How long to hold
steps.body:
- **Quarter note** (♩): 1 beat.
- **Half note** (𝅗𝅥): 2 beats. Count "1 2" while holding.
- **Whole note** (𝅝): 4 beats, a full measure of 4/4.

Keep the key down for the whole value, then release as the next note begins. The app mainly times when each note **starts**, but holding for the full length trains your counting and makes the music sound connected.

questions.prompt: How many beats does a half note get in 4/4?
questions.explanation: A half note is half of a whole note: 2 beats.

lessons.title: Eighth notes and rests
lessons.summary: Split the beat in two, and count silences.

steps.title: Eighth notes
steps.body:
An **eighth note** lasts half a beat, so two fit in one beat. Count them with "and": **1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &**. The numbers fall on the beat; the "&" falls exactly halfway between.

Single eighth notes have a flag; groups are joined by a **beam**.

diagram.rhythm: e e e e e e e e

steps.title: Rests
steps.body:
A **rest** is a measured silence. Each note value has a matching rest: **whole rest** (4 beats in 4/4), **half rest** (2), **quarter rest** (1), **eighth rest** (½).

Lift your finger off the key during a rest so the sound stops, and keep counting through it. Rests are part of the rhythm, not a pause in it.

diagram.caption: play, rest, play, rest | half note, half rest

lessons.title: Dotted notes and 3/4 time
lessons.summary: Add half a note's value with a dot, and count in threes.

steps.title: The dot
steps.body:
A **dot** after a note adds half of that note's value.

- **Dotted half note** = 2 + 1 = **3 beats**.
- **Dotted quarter note** = 1 + ½ = **1½ beats**, usually followed by an eighth note to complete two beats. Count it "1 (2) &": play on 1, hold through 2, play the eighth on the "&" of 2.

diagram.caption: dotted quarter + eighth, then a half note

steps.title: 3/4 time
steps.body:
In **3/4 time** there are **three** quarter-note beats per measure. Count **1 2 3, 1 2 3**, with a stronger beat 1. Waltzes and minuets are in 3/4.

A dotted half note fills a whole measure of 3/4.

diagram.rhythm: q q q h q h.

steps.title: A measure of 3/4, then a dotted half
steps.caption: Three quarters, half + quarter, then a dotted half: "1 2 3 | 1 2 3 | 1 2 3".
